2603.01712.tldr: FT-Dojo: an interactive benchmark for autonomous LLM fine-tuning — 13 tasks across 5 domains for end-to-end fine-tuning agents.
2603.01712.method: Interactive benchmark where an agent must curate data, configure training, and diagnose model behavior end-to-end, across 13 tasks in 5 domains.
results: Systematically studies end-to-end fine-tuning as an agent task, exposing where agents fail.
limitations: A benchmark, not a method; task coverage is still small.

2606.06473.tldr: An LLM multi-agent framework that evolves end-to-end ML algorithms, reaching 65.3% average medal rate on MLE-Bench in a 12-hour budget — best among compared agents at half the standard 24h runtime — and the best result on 11 of 15 AlphaEvolve math-optimization tasks.
2606.06473.method: Three coupled mechanisms per task (500 steps, 12h). A branch is a root-to-leaf trajectory of candidate solutions (3 initial drafts, max 5 branches plus 2 fusion). (1) Progressive MCGS: primary edges carry UCT selection and backpropagation; reference edges — never backpropagated — point from other branches' top nodes, so cross-branch transfer conditions generation on retrieved solutions, not scalar rewards. A soft switch w(t) decays 1.0→0.2, blending UCT exploration into Elite-Guided picks from the global top-3 by inverse rank; two-level stagnation detection (τ_branch=3, τ_global=6) triggers intra-branch evolution, cross-branch fusion, or multi-branch aggregation at the root. (2) Retrospective Memory: curated cold-start knowledge base plus a dynamic global store of per-node records (plan, outcome, metric, analysis), retrieved by BM25+FAISS fused via RRF at planning/debugging stages — records persist across the run, replacing memoryless scalar-only search. (3) Planner-coder decoupling: planner decides what/why at module level; coder implements via Base/Stepwise/Diff modes chosen by search state.
results: MLE-Bench (75 tasks, 12h budget, 3 seeds): 65.3% average medal rate, 34.7% gold, 100% valid submissions, 76.0% above-median — vs. best 24h baselines MARS+ 62.7% medal / 33.8% gold and AIBuildAI 63.1% / 25.8%; by complexity 80.3% low, 64.0% medium, 46.7% high.

AlphaEvolve's 15 math-optimization tasks: best result on 11 of 15 vs. AlphaEvolve, AlphaEvolve-v2, SimpleTES, TTT-Discover, and OpenEvolve (e.g., sums-differences problem 1: 1.1901774219 vs. AlphaEvolve's 1.1479889651; circle packing in a rectangle: 2.3658323759 vs. 2.3658321334).

Component ablation on MLE-Bench Lite (22 tasks): medal 81.82% full → 68.18% w/o Progressive MCGS, 68.18% w/o Retrospective Memory (the paper's cited 13.64% drop), 72.73% w/o adaptive code generation; beat ratio 88.39% vs. 79.91/81.90/84.14.

Search dynamics: effective active branches exp(H(π)) falls 4.8 → 2.8 over the run (vanilla MCTS flat at ~4.3); on representative tasks beat ratio reaches 98.2% vs. ~70% for vanilla MCTS, which plateaus early.

Mechanism-level ablation (9-task subset): removing intra-branch evolution drops medal 66.67% → 33.33% (largest single factor); removing the knowledge base or the global memory each drops it to 44.44%.
advantages: State-of-the-art MLE-Bench result at half the standard 24-hour budget (65.3% vs. MARS+ 62.7% and AIBuildAI 63.1%, both at 24h) with 100% valid submissions — an efficiency claim, not just a score claim.

Cross-domain check most MLE agents skip: unchanged, it beats specialized algorithm-discovery systems (AlphaEvolve, AlphaEvolve-v2, OpenEvolve) on 11/15 math tasks, evidence the search machinery generalizes past Kaggle.

Reference edges are a clean way to get cross-branch information flow without corrupting credit assignment — backpropagation stays strictly on primary edges — and every mechanism ablates positively, with intra-branch evolution isolated as the critical one.

Memory accumulates without extra reflection LLM calls: records are logged by a Result Parse Agent and retrieved by BM25+FAISS/RRF, unlike MARS/ROME-style reflection memory, and the two memory halves (static KB vs. dynamic store) are separately ablatable.
limitations: Expensive per task: up to 500 expansion steps over 12h on 21 vCPUs / 234GB RAM, an H200 GPU, and a frontier backbone (Gemini-3.1-Pro-preview); baseline numbers are taken from leaderboards or papers, so comparisons confound framework with different backbone LLMs and budgets.

The edge shrinks with difficulty: 46.7% medal on high-complexity tasks only ties AIBuildAI's 46.7% (at 24h), vs. 80.3% on low-complexity — most of the gain over MARS+ comes from medium tasks (64.0% vs. 60.5%).

The cold-start knowledge base is manually curated per task type from repositories and competition platforms, so part of performance is static human prior rather than self-evolved; the dynamic memory is task-scoped, not accumulated across tasks (ML-Master 2.0's cross-task caching is the contrast).
Ablation statistics are thin: 22 tasks (Lite) for component removal, 9 tasks for mechanism analysis, and some headline cells carry ±0.0 SEM over 3 seeds (gold rate, valid rate, high-complexity).
2606.06473.fits: Stage-8 descendant of AutoML-Zero/AlphaEvolve for whole-ML-algorithm discovery (the repo positions it as AutoMLGen's successor): it keeps the propose-execute-evaluate loop but adds machinery that makes long-horizon search persistent — graph reference edges for cross-branch reuse, an entropy schedule shifting exploration toward exploitation, run-length experience memory, and planner/coder decoupling.

2601.10657.tldr: PACEvolve diagnoses three failure modes of LLM-driven evolutionary search — context pollution, mode collapse, weak collaboration — and fixes them with hierarchical idea memory, momentum-triggered backtracking, and self-adaptive cross-island crossover, reaching state-of-the-art on symbolic regression, KernelBench, and Modded NanoGPT.
2601.10657.method: From 200+ 1000-step evolution runs the authors find append-only history contexts saturate with failed trials (context pollution), agents anchor to locally similar hypotheses (mode collapse), and static periodic crossover wastes parallel compute (weak collaboration). PACEvolve evolves candidate solutions (equations, GPU kernels, training code) via three mechanisms. HCM decouples idea generation from selection over a persistent idea pool (caps: 5 ideas, 20 hypotheses each): an LLM classifier merges conceptually duplicate ideas, caps trigger summarization and LLM pruning, and a permanent failure log preserves consistency by blocking rediscovery of dead ends. MBB computes scale-invariant Relative Progress R_t (fraction of remaining gap G_t = s_t − r closed), smoothed into momentum m_t by EWMA (β=0.85); when m_t < 0.001 the trajectory reverts to an ancestor state drawn from a power-law (α=1.5), resetting context. CE then samples backtrack vs. crossover from other islands with probability proportional to absolute-progress-based weights.
results: LLM-SR nonlinear-oscillator symbolic regression (Log10 NMSE, 10 runs × 1000 iterations, Gemini 2.5 Pro): PACEvolve-Multi best −8.24 / P75 −7.64 / mean −6.11 vs ShinkaEvolve −6.35 / −5.92 / −5.35, OpenEvolve −7.11 / −5.79 / −5.40, and non-LLM uDSR best −4.06; Multi finds 3 solutions below log10 NMSE −8.

KernelBench (16 kernels, 1000 iterations each, A100 40GB): beats the best KernelBench-leaderboard kernel on all 16, beats ShinkaEvolve on all 16 (PACE-Multi ≥ Single on 13/16, i.e. 81.25%), matches-or-beats OpenEvolve on 15/16 and CodeEvolve/ShinkaEvolve on 14/16; up to 17.38× over PyTorch (LayerNorm, 10.1ms → 0.581ms), though it loses to PyTorch on MLP/MatMul.

Modded NanoGPT (8×H100, Gemini 3 Pro): cuts time to val loss 3.28 on FineWeb from the heavily optimized v40 baseline 142.8s → 140.2s via data sharding/preloading, U-shaped skip-connection init (0.8→0.4→0.8), hyperparameter tuning, and dynamic context scheduling — on a benchmark already optimized from ~2700s (v1) to 142s.

Ablation (10 runs each): HCM lifts mean/best but worst runs still stall (a locally-optimal idea is never erased); adding MBB eliminates stalled trajectories yet slightly hurts best runs (exploration tax); adding CE recovers top-run performance while keeping the floor — full stack needed.
advantages: Real diagnosis, not anecdote: 200+ 1000-step runs show trajectories that fail to find low-NMSE solutions in the first few iterations rarely recover, with large variance across independent runs (Fig. 2) — grounding context pollution and mode collapse in measured search dynamics.
Each failure mode gets a matched, ablation-isolated fix: HCM's bi-level pruning cleans context, and MBB's progress-aware trigger removes the worst-run tail that context erasure alone cannot (§4.3).

The scale-invariant Relative Progress metric lets one stagnation trigger work across tasks without task-specific thresholds, unlike fixed-schedule resets in ShinkaEvolve/FunSearch-style loops that ignore search state.
Same scaffold achieves SOTA across three distinct domains — scientific equation discovery, GPU kernel optimization, and full-stack distributed training engineering — suggesting the recipe transfers.
limitations: By the paper's own ablation, backtracking 'slightly affected the best-performing processes' (exploration taxes exploitation), and CE only helps 'provided that at least one island discovers a promising direction' — joint all-island stagnation remains a risk.

No explicit limitations section; the authors flag KernelBench/Modded-NanoGPT world knowledge as 'questionable' (Table 5) since optimization strategies likely sit in LLM pretraining corpora, so gains may partly reflect retrieval rather than search.

Tasks need smooth rewards and cheap evaluation per the paper's own criteria; Modded NanoGPT needs 8 H100s and its gain is incremental (142.8s → 140.2s, conceded as 'this improvement looks incremental').

Mechanism assumes a known metric lower bound r and tuned constants (β=0.85, ε_rel=0.001, caps 5/20, power-law exponent 1.5); a sweep (Fig. 5) reports robustness but values are still benchmark-derived.
2601.10657.fits: Stage-9 prerequisite: open-ended evolution stalls without memory governance — long-horizon search needs structured, pruned idea memory plus a progress signal that decides when to abandon a line of work. Its diagnosis-first methodology (measure failure modes across 200+ runs, then derive the scaffold) pairs naturally with PACE-style diagnosis in this catalog.
2601.10657.reading: Read §2 (failure-mode study), §3.1–3.3 (HCM, MBB, CE with the Relative Progress equations), §4.3 (ablation), and Appendix A (case-study insights); Appendix B has pseudocode and hyperparameters (β=0.85, ε=0.001, caps 5/20).

openreview-higher-order-evolution-2024.tldr: Higher-order evolution: evolve the mutation rate, recursively the meta-mutation rate, up to a self-referential top-level parameter that modifies itself.
openreview-higher-order-evolution-2024.method: Evolves higher-order parameters (mutation rate → meta-mutation rate → … up to a self-referential top-level parameter that modifies itself), showing this improves robustness in Population-Based Training and Unsupervised Environment Design.
results: Self-referential mutation improves robustness to initial hyperparameters and enables complex adaptation in competitive multi-agent settings.
limitations: Small-scale domains (PBT/UED); self-referential levels are still bounded in practice.
openreview-higher-order-evolution-2024.fits: The evolutionary-computation counterpart to the Gödel Agent — the meta-parameters of evolution are themselves evolved, one step toward self-referential search.
openreview-higher-order-evolution-2024.reading: Read the higher-order/self-referential mutation definitions (§2–3) and the PBT/UED results.

1901.01753.tldr: POET: co-evolve environments and their solutions, transferring solutions between niches — an endless self-generated curriculum of stepping stones.
1901.01753.method: Co-evolves a population of environments and their specialized solutions; solutions transfer between niches, and the system continually generates more complex/diverse environments.
results: Finds solutions to problems it never directly targeted (stepping-stone transfer), including a hard-to-discover bipedal walker via indirect transfer.
limitations: Simple 2D-locomotion domains; the open-ended loop is hard to stabilize and scale.
1901.01753.fits: The canonical 'generate your own problems' system — POWERPLAY made evolutionary and open-ended; the lineage behind UED and modern self-generated curricula.
1901.01753.reading: Read the co-evolution + transfer mechanism (§3) and the stepping-stone result (§4).

agent-zero.what: A general-purpose agent framework that gives the agent a full Linux computer — a Dockerized desktop, annotated browser, document cowork, skills/plugins, and a bridge back to your host.
architecture: Dockerized Linux desktop + browser with DOM annotation for real computer/GUI control.
Projects, skills, and plugins as persistent capabilities the agent composes.
Host bridge lets the agent act on and coordinate with the user's own machine.
agent-zero.run: Docker-based: `docker compose up` (see the Quick Start in the README) launches the desktop + browser; add your LLM API key.
agent-zero.note: An 'extensible substrate' — the harness *is* a whole computer. Study it for how an OS-level workspace generalizes far beyond a chat loop.

deepseek-harness.what: DeepSeek's open-source agent harness, built on an everything-is-a-plugin architecture (powered by Cordis), with web and CLI runtimes.
architecture: Everything-is-a-plugin: tools, memory, and orchestration are all plugins composed via Cordis (spatiotemporal composability).
Web UI + CLI launch modes; developer preview with a documented safety notice.
deepseek-harness.run: `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web` starts the Web UI at http://127.0.0.1:3080 (Node.js required).
deepseek-harness.note: A production-grade harness from a frontier lab — the plugin architecture is the reusable idea (contrast with monolithic harnesses).

openclaw.what: A self-hosted personal assistant that runs on your own devices and lives in your chats (Node.js, MIT).
architecture: Runs locally across your devices rather than in a hosted cloud.
Chat-native: plugs into existing messaging surfaces as an assistant.
Distributed as `openclaw` on npm; Node.js runtime.
openclaw.run: `npm install -g openclaw` (or `npx openclaw`) then follow onboarding; Node.js required.
openclaw.note: The 'assistant on your own hardware' substrate — useful for studying how self-improvement is shaped by local, persistent execution.

pi.what: Pi's agent harness — a monorepo whose centerpiece is a self-extensible coding agent.
architecture: Monorepo packages: `pi-coding-agent` (interactive CLI), `pi-agent-core` (agent runtime with tool calling + state), `pi-ai` (unified multi-provider LLM API).
The self-extensible coding agent builds on the runtime to extend its own capabilities.
pi.note: A clean split of runtime / LLM-API / coding-agent — the layered design makes 'self-extension' concrete (the agent modifies its own tool set).

hermes-agent.what: Nous Research's Hermes agent and desktop app — a general-purpose local agent with a full desktop interface.
architecture: Agent runtime + desktop client (macOS/Windows/Linux).
MIT-licensed; docs at hermes-agent.nousresearch.com.
hermes-agent.run: Install the desktop app or run from source per the README/docs.
hermes-agent.note: A usability-focused harness — good for seeing how memory/tools surface in a real product rather than a research scaffold.

seal.what: SEAL (Self-Adapting LLMs) trains models via RL to generate *self-edits* — their own finetuning data and update directives — in response to new inputs.
architecture: RL loop where the model proposes edits (finetuning data + update directives) to itself.
Two domains: general-knowledge (absorb new facts) and few-shot (adapt to new tasks).
MIT CSAIL; code + data for both domains in the repo.
seal.run: Python; `git clone`, set up a conda/venv (README §Setup), then run the domain scripts.
seal.note: A model-level self-improvement substrate: the model writes the *data and update instructions* for its own adaptation — a concrete bridge between weight-space and data-space RSI.

letta-code.what: A stateful agent harness where agents have memory, identity, and experience — and can rewrite their own memory, skills, prompts, and the harness itself via 'mods'.
architecture: Stateful agents with persistent memory/identity/experience over long horizons.
Self-modification: agents rewrite their own memory, skills, prompts, and harness (mods).
Surfaces: CLI, desktop app, browser (chat.letta.com), and messaging channels.
letta-code.run: `npx @letta-ai/letta-code` for the CLI; desktop app available for macOS/Windows/Linux.
letta-code.note: One of the most direct 'harness that modifies itself' products — study the mods mechanism for how self-modification is scoped safely.

memento-skills.what: Memento-S: a skill-centric agent runtime where skills are the unit of capability — retrieved, executed, authored, and repaired in deployment. Agents design agents via guarded skill evolution; the accompanying study shows deployment-time skill learning (frozen weights) improving GAIA and HLE over reflective rounds.
architecture: Skills as SKILL.md + scripts directories under builtin/skills/ (filesystem, web-search, skill-creator, uv-pip-install), loaded by core/skill/loader/, modeled in core/skill/schema.py (pydantic Skill with JSON-schema parameters, default a single natural-language `request`), persisted through db/file/vector backends in core/skill/store/.

4-phase pipeline in core/memento_s/phases/: intent.py → planning.py (the *Architect* emits a TaskPlan of PlanSteps at single-skill granularity with input_from dataflow) → execution/ (multi-step ReAct loop split into runner, tool_handler, step_boundary, guarded by hooks/ loop_detector, sandbox_audit, policy/tool_gate) → reflection.py (the *Supervisor* decides continue/replan/finalize/ASK_USER) and finalize.py.

Agents design agents in two places: core/skill/evolution/engine.py — transactional write phase that attributes a failed trace to one skill (confidence-scored), LLM-rewrites files in an isolated copy, gates it on static/unit/synthetic-judge tests, then deploys atomically or rolls back — plus builtin/skills/skill-creator/ (analyzer/comparator/grader sub-agents, run_eval.py, package_skill.py) for authoring new skills from scratch.

Routing over the library via core/skill/retrieval/ (local_recall BM25+vector, qwen_recall.py Qwen3/Memento-Qwen embeddings, remote_recall, multi_recall fusion) feeding core/memento_s/skill_dispatch/ (hallucination_guard, post_install); unified tools/registry.py wraps tools/atomics/ + MCP; surfaces: memento agent CLI, Flet memento-gui desktop app, core/skill/market.py cloud catalogue with downloader/github.py, and daemon/dream/ consolidator that mines sessions into skill candidates.
advantages: The only catalog entry where self-modification is transactional: attribution → isolated file-level rewrite → static/unit/synthetic gates → atomic deploy or rollback, with audit history — a worked answer to 'how does an agent safely edit its own capabilities', vs. code-as-skill systems (Voyager, AgentFactory) that write skills without candidate gating.

Deployment-time learning with frozen parameters (θ frozen, behaviour stored in external skill memory M): the GAIA/HLE round-over-round gains make it a concrete substrate for studying skill-memory growth curves instead of fine-tuning.

Ships as a real product, not a benchmark script — CLI, Windows/macOS desktop app, IM gateways, Skill Market — so you can test whether learned skills persist and transfer across live sessions, and compare its SKILL.md packaging (Anthropic-compatible, per THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES) against OpenClaw's deployment-first take.
memento-skills.run: git clone https://github.com/Memento-Teams/Memento-Skills.git && cd Memento-Skills && python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -e . && memento doctor && memento agent  # configure ~/memento_s/config.json (llm profile + TAVILY_API_KEY); GUI: memento-gui; or desktop app from memento.run/release
memento-skills.note: Open core/skill/evolution/engine.py plus docs/QWEN_ROUTER_AND_SKILL_EVOLUTION.md for the guarded write loop; phases/planning.py vs phases/reflection.py for the replan decision; builtin/skills/skill-creator/ for the meta-skill loop. Compare its transactional skill repair and SKILL.md format with Voyager/AgentFactory code-as-skill.

reef.what: First open-source infrastructure for continual self-improving agents: an OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible serving layer that records interactions, matches feedback to receipts, trains weights (Slime/SGLang) or evolves harness text (Reefine), and publishes only evaluation-passing updates as versioned releases while serving continues.
architecture: Serve-Observe-Grow-Commit loop mapped to real modules (README table): reef/service/ takes OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible requests (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/messages) and records interactions; reef/storage/records.py stores AgentRecords; reef/train/processors/ match reported feedback to eligibility; reef/recipe/ + reef/train/ produce the update; reef/train/evaluation/ + reef/artifact/ gate and publish it.

Feedback is receipt-based: every response carries an x-reef-agent-record-id header; POST /reef/report attaches {score, feedback, references:[receipt]} validated against schemas in reef/core/reports/ (scored_rollout, teacher_context); the x-reef-scenario request header creates or selects the scenario whose recipe decides what evolves — requests never pick recipes.

Backends are pluggable: reef/train/slime_backend/ (Megatron LoRA adapters, Ray executors, weight_updaters) and tinker_backend/ train weights; reef/train/cordis_backend/ proposes harness Mutations; recipes (sao, tttd, gepa, meta_harness, openclawrl, skillclaw) live in the recipes/ cookbook, selected by dotted class reference and not shipped in the wheel.

Versioned delivery: reef/artifact/ keeps an immutable parent-linked release chain (fork, publish with expected_parent, staged commit_release, git+LFS) and rejected candidates never move the serving release; reef/train/evaluation/evaluators.py ships RegressionCheckMixin — select only while the metric stays within margin of the best so far, so serving holds last selected weights — and reef/surface/ delivers accepted artifacts to harness adapters (pi, claude, codex, opencode, terminus).
advantages: The only substrate here that learns under live traffic: serving and training share the deployment, updated weights sync in without a restart, and a rejected candidate leaves the current release serving — unlike offline search loops (RRSI) or batch RL frameworks, both of which stop the world to improve.

One receipt/report plumbing over two artifacts: model weights (SAO continual learning; TTT-Discover test-time training with measured TriMul, circle-packing and Erdos minimum-overlap results) or harness text (Reefine writes a change as a skill, rules entry, agent command, or pi extension and test-runs it under bwrap/pasta sandboxing) — weight-level and harness-level RSI in one deployment.

Non-regression is a first-class policy, not a convention: each candidate-evaluation plugin implements evaluate() and decide() in one contract, with best-checkpoint selection running online against the deployment's own traffic.
reef.run: Python 3.12+, git-lfs required for artifacts. `uv venv && source .venv/bin/activate && uv pip install reef-infra`, then a pure inference server: `uv run reef serve --inference.model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct`. Harness evolution (no GPUs): `reef serve --recipe reefine --inference.upstream-url http://127.0.0.1:11434 --inference.upstream-model gemma4:26b`, then `reef-pi evolve "..."`. Weight training adds `uv pip install -e ".[slime]" && uv pip install --no-deps --group runtime`.
reef.note: Trace the core loop from reef/service/app.py through reef/artifact/release_chain.py; read train/evaluation/evaluators.py (RegressionCheckMixin is the online non-regression gate) and compare recipes/sao/ (weights) with reef/recipe/reefine/evolution.py (harness) — the same loop over two artifact types.

autoresearch.what: Karpathy's experiment: hand an agent a small but real LLM-training setup and let it improve it autonomously overnight.
architecture: Agent modifies training code, trains ~5 minutes, checks whether the result improved, keeps or discards, repeats.
Built on a simplified single-GPU nanochat implementation.
Logs experiments so you wake up to a history — and hopefully a better model.
autoresearch.run: Python; single-GPU; see README for the nanochat-based setup.
autoresearch.note: A deliberately *small, real* self-improvement loop — the minimal reproducible 'AI improving its own training code'. Note: distinct from the AutoResearch *paper* (2608.17906).

evolutionary-model-merge.what: Sakana's Evolutionary Model Merge — evolve recipes for merging multiple foundation models in weight space (no training).
architecture: Evolution (CMA-ES) searches layer-wise merge ratios and permutations.
Combines several open models into one merged model with each's strengths (e.g., Japanese + math + code).
Hub for released merged models (e.g., EvoLLM-JP-v1-7B) + evaluation code.
evolutionary-model-merge.run: Python; evaluation scripts + released models on Hugging Face (SakanaAI org).
evolutionary-model-merge.note: Model-level self-improvement by *recombination* — improving an AI by evolving how existing weights are mixed, cheaper than gradient descent.

openevolve.what: An open-source evolutionary coding agent — turns an LLM into an autonomous code optimizer that discovers better algorithms.
architecture: Evolutionary loop: LLM proposes code variants, an evaluator scores them, the best survive and seed the next generation.
From random search to state-of-the-art — refines programs against a fitness signal.
Distributed as `openevolve` on PyPI with system-message guides.
openevolve.run: `pip install openevolve`; see Quick Start and Examples in the README.
openevolve.note: The 'LLM + evaluator + evolution' recipe (FunSearch/AlphaEvolve) packaged as a drop-in library — the fastest way to *run* an evolutionary coding loop.

agentfactory.what: Official code for AgentFactory (ACL 2026 System Demo, arXiv 2603.18000) — a self-evolving agent framework that saves successful task solutions as executable Python subagents, refines them from execution feedback, and exports the library to other frameworks.
architecture: Subagents are plain Python modules with a standardized main(query) entry point returning {answer, summary}, stored under skills/subagents/ with a SKILL.md doc each — pure code, portable to any Python-capable system.

The Meta-Agent orchestrates via meta-skills: create_subagent → run_subagent → modify_subagent (exact old/new snippet replacement) → finish; finish persists the library and carries a supersedes field so major rewrites delete the old skill.

Three skill tiers — meta orchestration skills, tool skills (Serper search, Jina reader, Playwright browser, shell), and the growing subagent library — plus a Workspace Manager giving per-task isolated execution so edits can't corrupt the shared library.

Refinement is feedback-driven and enforces genericity: create prompts ban hardcoded task specifics (all specifics must be extracted from the query via call_llm at runtime), and modify-vs-create rules separate surgical fixes from supersedes rewrites.
advantages: Ships recorded trajectories (trajectory/qq_music, tencent_doc, readme) so you can watch a subagent library accrete without running anything — the third Tencent Docs run directly reuses the audio_transcriber subagent born in the QQ Music runs.

Executable experience is deployable as-is: prompt4cc.txt exports the saved library into Claude Code, and subagents port to LangChain/AutoGen; README's 30-task eval reports reuse dropping orchestrator output tokens to 2,971 vs ReAct's 7,022 (Opus 4.6, up to 57% savings).

The whole create→run→modify→save loop is inspectable in eight root-level Python files (meta_agent.py, meta_tools.py, run.py, tools.py...) plus the skills/meta SKILL.md docs — no framework magic hiding the mechanism.
agentfactory.run: `conda create -n agentfactory python=3.12 && pip install openai requests playwright flask flask_cors`; fill .env (MODEL_PROTOCOL, LLM key/url/model, SERPER_API_KEY, JINA_API_KEY) and replace <Absolute_Path_to_AgentFactory> in the question files; then `python run.py --question-file data/questions/questions_round1.jsonl` (flags: --human-confirm, --no-save). Web demo: `python3 web_interface/app.py --port 5050`.
agentfactory.note: Cross-read with the 2603.18000 paper card. Read skills/meta/*/SKILL.md for the loop contract, then diff trajectory/*/first_time.json vs second_time.json to see reuse in action. Note the generality mandate: saved subagent code must never hardcode task-specific details.

dgm.what: Official implementation of the Darwin Gödel Machine (arXiv 2505.22954, Sakana AI + UBC): a coding agent that rewrites its own codebase, validates every candidate self-modification on SWE-bench/Polyglot in Docker, and archives each compiled variant as a parent future variants build on.
architecture: Outer loop (`DGM_outer.py`): up to `--max_generation 80` generations, each spawning `--selfimprove_size 2` parallel improvement attempts. `choose_selfimproves` picks a parent from the archive plus a target — a 25% roll each for `solve_empty_patches` (only if ≥10% of the parent's eval came back empty), `solve_stochasticity`, or `solve_contextlength`, else a random unresolved SWE-bench instance; an o1 diagnoser (`diagnose_model='o1-2024-12-17'`) converts that parent's failure logs into the `problem_statement` handed to the improver.

Improvement is a patch, not a commit: each attempt builds a fresh `dgm` Docker container, replays the entire ancestral chain of `model_patch.diff` files (`get_model_patch_paths` walks `parent_commit` links back to `initial`, applying them with `patch -p1`), then runs `coding_agent.py --self_improve` (bash + edit tools, 30-min timeout) whose edits are captured by `diff_versus_commit` as a new `model_patch.diff` against the DGM's own source.

Archive is a scored phylogenetic tree, not a leaderboard: every node stores accuracy plus `parent_commit`; the default parent sampler `score_child_prop` weights nodes by sigmoid(10·(score−0.5)) × 1/(children+1) — objective quality times novelty pressure. Default `--update_archive keep_all` keeps every child passing `is_compiled_self_improve` (non-empty patch, full subset actually evaluated) even when it didn't improve; `keep_better` (≥ initial score − `--eval_noise 0.1`) and the `--run_baseline` ablations (`no_darwin` = greedy always-latest-commit, `no_selfimprove`) isolate what open-endedness buys.

Staged empirical gate: children are scored on a small SWE-bench Verified subset, promoted to a medium subset only at ≥0.4 resolution (`test_more_threshold`), and get the full evaluation only above `get_full_eval_threshold` — the second-highest fully-evaluated archive score, floored at 0.4. `--polyglot` swaps in `coding_agent_polyglot.py` and the Aider Polyglot harness.
advantages: The substrate where the object under improvement is the improver's own executable source: the archived patch edits the tool/loop code that produces the next patches, so tool, prompt, and control-flow improvements compound across generations.

A unusually clean open-endedness control: `--run_baseline no_darwin` ablates exactly the archive-based parent selection while holding the improver fixed, and `keep_all` vs `keep_better` tests whether retaining 'failed but compiled' cousins — not just hill-climbing — drives the gains.

Ships the full experiment apparatus: `initial/` reference eval logs defining the starting agent's baseline, staged small→medium→full evaluation to keep Dockerized SWE-bench runs affordable, and the paper's complete model-output logs on Google Drive.
dgm.run: Docker + Python venv; export OPENAI_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. `pip install -r requirements.txt`; in `swe_bench/` clone SWE-bench at pinned commit `dc4c087c2b9e4cefebf2e3d201d27e36` and `pip install -e .`; `python -m polyglot.prepare_polyglot_dataset`; then `python DGM_outer.py` (default output `output_dgm/`; `--polyglot` for the Polyglot run).
dgm.note: Read `choose_selfimproves` and `update_archive` in DGM_outer.py — the score×novelty parent sampler and keep_all archive — against the `no_darwin` baseline, then `self_improve_step.py`'s container-per-attempt patch replay. README warning: it executes untrusted model-generated code.

godel-agent.what: Gödel Agent — a self-referential agent whose behavior is code it can inspect and rewrite: its actions, prompts and solver are Python it reads, patches at runtime, and re-evaluates in a loop (arXiv 2410.04444).
architecture: src/agent_module.py is the whole agent (~724 lines): Agent(AgentBase) plus its own tool schema list agent.action_functions — action_read_logic (inspect.getsource on itself), action_adjust_logic (exec + setattr on the live module/class, keeping a __source__ map so rewritten methods stay readable), action_run_code, action_evaluate_on_task.

Loop in src/main.py: reinit() feeds the agent its own solver source, then evolve() prompts o3 with tools=agent.action_functions, tool_choice='required' — the model must act; action_counter['evolve'] >= 100 hard-exits the run.

Validation is accuracy-gated checkpointing: action_evaluate_on_task calls task.evaluate(solver); only when accuracy beats task_mgsm.last_test_acc does logic.store_all_logic() dump the current in-memory agent to results/<task>/agent_module/ (drop_80.892.txt, gpqa_0.3494.txt, mmlu_0.7087.txt, mgsm_0.6425.txt).

Eval harnesses src/task_{mgsm,mmlu,gpqa,drop}.py are adapted from ADAS; src/goal_prompt.md tells the model literally that it is the self_evolving_agent instance of Agent in module agent_module — self-reference by address, not metaphor.
advantages: Purest code-as-identity artifact in this catalog: no outer harness owns the improvement loop — the agent edits the very module it executes from, so monkey-patching, runtime guardrails and self-inspection are all directly observable in one readable file.

results/ ships the evolved agent per benchmark, so you can diff what a run actually changed (e.g. the DROP solver it grew from a one-shot gpt-4o-mini prompt into a 5-sample self-consistency ensemble) before spending API money.

Edit-time safety is explicit and small: what the framework forbids (rewriting action_call_llm / action_call_json_format_llm, time.sleep in solver, logging) is exactly the guardrail-boundary question RRSI cares about.
godel-agent.run:
git clone https://github.com/Arvid-pku/Godel_Agent.git && cd Godel_Agent && pip install -r requirements.txt  # deps: numpy, tqdm, pandas, openai==1.2.0, backoff; put an OpenAI key in src/key.env
python src/main.py  # README: 'You can adjust the task in the agent_module.py file.'
godel-agent.note: Read results/*/agent_module/ first — the evolved DROP/MMLU solvers show what the loop actually finds. Then study action_adjust_logic's guardrails and the accuracy-gated store_all_logic checkpoint. Theory-side companion to DGM; here self-reference is literal: the agent is the module it edits.

hyperagents.what: HyperAgents (DGM-Hyperagents, DGM-H) — code for arXiv 2603.19461: a task agent and a meta agent live in one editable program, so the improver rewrites both the task-solving code and its own improvement mechanism, generalizing the Darwin Gödel Machine beyond coding.
architecture: meta_agent.py / task_agent.py — the self-referential pair, both subclasses of AgentSystem (agent/base_agent.py): MetaAgent.forward(repo_path, eval_path, iterations_left) issues exactly one instruction — 'Modify any part of the codebase at `{repo_path}`' — via chat_with_agent with all bash/edit tools (agent/tools/); TaskAgent is the object-level agent being improved. run_meta_agent.py then git-resets domains/ back to the base commit (reset_paths_to_commit) so the eval harness can't be gamed, and saves the rest as model_patch.diff.

generate_loop.py — the evolution driver: per generation it builds a Docker container (image `hyperagents`), replays the parent's full lineage of diffs (get_patch_files → apply_diffs_container), runs the meta agent (6h timeout), requires a non-empty model_patch.diff plus a compilation check (run_commands_to_check_compilation), then staged-evals on a small subset (gate: every domain scores > 0) before the full eval via domains/harness.py + domains/report; accepted nodes append to archive.jsonl with metadata.json per gen_*/.

Open-ended search over the archive: utils/gl_utils.py::select_parent (default --parent_selection score_child_prop — score-proportional but inversely proportional to children, keeping the space open); --edit_select_parent hands the selection mechanism itself to the meta agent (select_next_parent.py, run inside a container via utils.run_select_next_parent); ensemble.py scores the whole archive as one agent; --meta_patch_files with --reset_task_agent/--reset_meta_agent drive the cross-run, cross-domain transfer experiments.

domains/ are swappable evaluators with train/val/test splits — paper_review (default in setup_initial.sh), search_arena, balrog_{babyai,babaisai,minihack,nle}, genesis_go2walking/hop/walkback (robot reward-function design), imo_grading, imo_proof, polyglot (SWE-bench, one Docker per task); baselines/ ships dgm/coding_agent.py plus no_selfimprove/no_archive ablations; agent/llm.py wires litellm (default anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929).
advantages: The only substrate in this catalog where the search machinery itself sits inside the search space: parent selection, staged eval and ensembling are plain Python files next to the agents, so you can watch metacognitive improvements (the paper's persistent memory, performance tracking) land as diffs in archive.jsonl and check they transfer across domains and accumulate across runs — evidence DGM's coding-only task/self-mod alignment cannot produce.

One loop, many domains: the same generate_loop.py improves LLM graders (imo_grading), game agents (Balrog), reward functions (Genesis Go2) and SWE-bench patches (polyglot), with dgm / no_selfimprove / no_archive baselines wired through the identical harness — the cleanest available testbed for whether meta-level gains generalize beyond coding.

Honesty by construction: the evaluator is quarantined from the improver (domains/ reset after every meta-agent run), candidates must compile before scoring, and staged small-sample evals gate the expensive full evals — a concrete template for safe-ish untrusted-code RSI loops.
hyperagents.run:
echo 'OPENAI_API_KEY=...
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...
GEMINI_API_KEY=...' > .env  # README setup
python3.12 -m venv venv_nat && source venv_nat/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt
docker build --network=host -t hyperagents .
bash ./setup_initial.sh
python generate_loop.py --domains paper_review  # script documents all args and baselines
hyperagents.note: Start at run_meta_agent.py: the domains/ git-reset is what keeps evals honest while everything else is fair game. Then generate_loop.py's staged-eval gate and gl_utils.select_parent's score_child_prop. Watch archive.jsonl grow and read gen_*/agent_output/meta_agent_chat_history.md — the transcript of the improver improving itself. DGM baseline: baselines/dgm/.

sia.what: Official implementation of arXiv 2605.27276: a Meta-Agent writes the initial task agent, a Feedback-Agent rewrites it every generation from execution logs, and a separate --focus weights mode RL-tunes the task model's weights via tinker-cookbook.
architecture: sia/orchestrator.py (967 lines) runs the loop: setup_run_directory makes runs/run_{id}/venv/ plus gen_{n}/ dirs; the meta-agent writes gen_1/target_agent.py; each generation the target executes (logging agent_execution.json), evaluate.py scores it against data/private/, and the feedback agent reads runs/run_{id}/context.md evolution history before writing target_agent.py + improvement.md into gen_{n+1}/ — weights mode early-stops on a COMPLETED file.

Two focus modes split the paper's W+H claim: --focus harness (default) has the feedback agent rewrite target_agent.py (prompt/code changes only); --focus weights instead makes the meta-agent emit train.py implementing tinker-cookbook Env/EnvGroupBuilder/RLDataset, executed by tinker_cookbook.rl.train.main() (GRPO via the Tinker API, TINKER_API_KEY required, rollouts sandboxed by --training_sandbox modal|sandboxfusion).

The improvement policy is literally prompt text in sia/prompts.py: build_meta_prompt / _build_weights_meta_prompt / build_feedback_prompt — including a mandated majority-voting (self-consistency) reward workaround so rewards keep variance when ground truth is hidden, and instructions to read context.md and not repeat failed approaches from earlier generations.

Tasks are directories, not code: data/public/ (task.md, evaluate.py) vs held-out data/private/; four bundled (gpqa, lawbench, longcot-chess, spaceship-titanic), BYO via --task_dir, or bootstrap any MLE-Bench competition with sia/prepare_mlebench_dataset.py. Agent backends are pluggable in sia/agent_impls/ (claude = Claude Agent SDK, openhands, pydantic-ai), selected with JSON provider/profile files under sia/defaults/{providers,profiles}/ (Tinker, Nebius, OpenRouter, ...).
advantages: The only catalog substrate where one pipeline optimizes harness and weights as switchable arms of the same loop — you can run harness-only, weights-only, and combined on the same task/evaluator and attribute the gains, which the paper's LawBench (45%→70.1%) and TriMul (14x kernel speedup) tables do per-domain.

Anti-gaming is engineered in, not hoped for: private/public data split enforced by the task layout, docs/evaluator_design.md on metric robustness, finite-timeout rules baked into target-agent prompts, and docker --sandbox (no network) for untrusted generated code.

Highly reproducible and inspectable: pip-installable (sia-agent on PyPI), per-run venv, a sia web dashboard replaying every generation's code, prompts, improvement.md and accuracy-across-generations chart — the cleanest substrate for studying why each rewrite helped or didn't.
sia.run: python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install 'sia-agent[claude]' && export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="..." && sia run --task gpqa --max_gen 5 --run_id 1    # weights mode: export TINKER_API_KEY=... && sia run --task gpqa --max_gen 5 --run_id 1 --focus weights --training_sandbox modal
sia.note: Read sia/prompts.py first — the whole improvement policy is prompt text, and the weights-mode meta prompt is a tinker-cookbook RL tutorial that makes the agent author train.py. Then orchestrator.py's run_generation. Study context.md: it is the memory that stops the loop repeating failed edits.

ace.what: ACE (Agentic Context Engineering) — code for arXiv 2510.04618: treats the whole LLM context as an evolving playbook of ID'd, helpful/harmful-counted bullets, self-improved by a Generator/Reflector/Curator loop making structured incremental delta updates — no weight updates, no full-prompt rewrites.
architecture: ace/ace.py — the ACE orchestrator class with run(mode='offline'|'online'|'eval_only'); instantiates the three roles from ace/core/: Generator, Reflector, Curator, plus an optional BulletpointAnalyzer (embedding-similarity dedup, threshold 0.90) over providers sambanova/together/openai/commonstack (default model DeepSeek-V3.1).

playbook_utils.py — deterministic merge layer: each bullet is a parseable line '[str-00001] helpful=5 harmful=0 :: advice' under 7 fixed ## sections (STRATEGIES & INSIGHTS, FORMULAS & CALCULATIONS, COMMON MISTAKES TO AVOID, ...); apply_curator_operations() applies ADD-only deltas with system-assigned global IDs (UPDATE/MERGE/DELETE/CREATE_META are documented stubs), update_bullet_counts() maintains the counters.

ace/prompts/curator.py — CURATOR_PROMPT / CURATOR_PROMPT_NO_GT emit pure-JSON operation lists (type/section/content/reasoning); a second CURATOR_OPERATIONS_AGGREGATION_PROMPT pass synthesizes overlapping ADDs into fewer, more specific ones before application — the grow-and-refine mechanism that prevents context collapse.

eval/finance/run.py (FiNER, XBRL formula), eval/mind2web/ and eval/mind2web2/, ace-appworld as a git submodule; CLI: uv run python -m eval.finance.run --task_name finer --mode offline --playbook_token_budget 80000 --use_bulletpoint_analyzer; each run writes results/ace_run_<ts>_<task>_<mode>/ with best_playbook.txt, bullet_usage_log.jsonl, curator_operations_diff.jsonl.
advantages: The one repo in this catalog where the self-improved artifact is the context itself, not code or harness — a direct open-source baseline against GEPA and Dynamic Cheatsheet (+10.6% AppWorld, +8.6% finance, ~86.9% lower adaptation latency), and the working complement to Voyager's code-skill library in prompt space.

Cleanest available reference implementation of collapse-resistant memory growth: JSON delta ops applied by deterministic non-LLM code (apply_curator_operations), system-assigned bullet IDs, helpful/harmful counters, then LLM aggregation + similarity dedup for pruning — the exact discipline any RSI harness with unboundedly growing notes needs.

Self-supervised by construction: reflector works from execution feedback alone (CURATOR_PROMPT_NO_GT, --no_ground_truth), and the same loop runs offline (train/val epochs) or online (update every --online_eval_frequency samples) with only 3 DataProcessor methods required to port a new domain.
ace.run:
git clone https://github.com/ace-agent/ace.git && cd ace && curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh && uv sync && cp .env.example .env  # add a provider key, then:
uv run python -m eval.finance.run --task_name finer --mode offline --save_path results   # or --mode online / eval_only --initial_playbook_path results/ace_run_.../best_playbook.txt
ace.note: Read ace/prompts/curator.py next to playbook_utils.apply_curator_operations and a run's curator_operations_diff.jsonl: the delta-op discipline (ADD-only, system-assigned IDs, aggregation pass) is what stops context collapse. Contrast bullet helpful/harmful counters with Voyager's skill library — prompt-space evolution, not code-space.

alma.what: ALMA (Automated meta-Learning of Memory designs for Agentic systems) — a Meta Agent searches open-endedly over memory designs expressed as executable Python, evaluating each in AlfWorld/TextWorld/BabaisAI/MiniHack and archiving winners by reward, replacing hand-engineered agent memory (G-Memory, ReasoningBank, Dynamic Cheatsheet) with domain-specialized learned designs.
architecture: core/meta_agent.py — MetaAgent.forward() is the search loop: analyze_memo_structure() reflects on a sampled design's source + eval logs, generate_new_code() implements the proposal, examine_new_code() verifies with up to 3 reflect-and-repair trials (build_reflection_prompt on the error), then the design is evaluated and its reward/parentage logged; run_main.py drives it with --meta_model gpt-5 --execution_model gpt-5-nano --status train.

core/memo_manager.py — Memo_Manager keeps the archive as memo_archive/{task_type}/memo_structure_{SHA}.py files keyed by an 8-char SHA in memo_db; update_reward() sigmoid-normalizes against the measured no_mem baseline, and select_structure() samples up to 5 parents per step via softmax(final_score/tau=0.5) minus alpha*log(visit_time) — a quality/diversity bandit with parent + improve_score lineage per design.

evals/agents/memo_structure.py — a design subclasses MemoStructure / Sub_memo_layer: a database plus arbitrary layers each implementing retrieve()/update(), composed freely via general_retrieve(recorder)/general_update(recorder); learned designs ship real machinery (langchain_chroma vector stores, FINCH clustering, networkx graphs), while memo_archive/baseline/ holds the human baselines it must beat (g_memory, pure_insights, insights_traj_sim, similarity, no_mem).

eval_in_container.py + envs_docker/ — every rollout executes model-generated memory code inside Docker: one ALFWorld image (envs_docker/alfworld/image_build.sh) and one shared BALROG image for TextWorld/BabaisAI/MiniHack (envs_docker/BALROG/image_build.sh); per-domain adapters live in envs_archive/{task}_envs.py + prompts/ + configs/. README reports the learned design beating all manual baselines on all four domains (12.3 vs 6.1 no-memory; 53.9 vs 41.1), with ICLR 2026 workshop orals (RSI + MemAgents).
advantages: The searched object is the memory architecture itself — schema, retrieval keys, and update policy as one evolvable Python file — not prompts or harness code: it is the meta-level above this catalog's memory baselines (G-Memory, Dynamic Cheatsheet, ACE playbooks), and it discovers which of those abstractions to re-invent per domain.

Learned designs are portable artifacts: a winning memory is a single memo_structure_{SHA}.py plus downloadable logs, so --memo_SHA g-memory or a learned SHA re-evaluates a design without re-running the expensive search (gpt-5 meta-agent over gpt-5-nano executors).

Purpose-built continual-learning testbed: --status eval_in_distribution vs eval_out_of_distribution measures whether a learned design transfers under task shift, against a measured no-memory baseline — the cleanest setup here for asking whether learned memory generalizes or overfits its training tasks.
alma.run:
git clone https://github.com/zksha/alma.git && cd alma && conda create -n alma python=3.11 && conda activate alma && pip install -r requirements.txt && add OPENAI_API_KEY to .env; build an env image: cd envs_docker/alfworld && bash image_build.sh  (or envs_docker/BALROG/image_build.sh once, shared by TextWorld/BabaisAI/MiniHack); then:
python run_main.py --rollout_type batched --meta_model gpt-5 --execution_model gpt-5-nano --batch_max_update_concurrent 10 --batch_max_retrieve_concurrent 10 --task_type alfworld --status train --train_size 30   # testing.sh / training.sh hold per-domain configs
alma.note: Read core/meta_agent_prompt.py's build_analysis_prompt and build_reflection_prompt — they show how eval logs and stack traces become concrete design edits. Then diff memo_archive/baseline/memo_structure_g_memory.py (Chroma + FINCH + networkx) against a learned design from the Drive link to see what search actually changed. README warns: it executes model-generated code — sandbox it.

continual-harness.what: Continual Harness — reset-free online self-improvement (arXiv 2605.09998, Gemini Plays Pokémon lineage): one continuous Pokémon episode where an LLM Refiner rewrites the agent's own prompt, sub-agents, skills, and memory in place, mid-episode.
architecture: agents/utils/harness_evolver.py — the HarnessEvolver class runs four failure-isolated passes (_evolve_prompt / _evolve_subagents / _evolve_skills / _evolve_memory) over the recent trajectory window, exposed to the agent as a single evolve_harness tool (--scaffold continualharness --enable-prompt-optimization); adaptive cadence: 25-step warmup, every 25 steps for the first 200, then every 100.

Component stores with per-entry mutation history — utils/stores/{memory,skills,subagents}.py; the repo ships a real evolved artifact (PokemonRed-GBC/bootstrap_source/: EVOLVED_ORCHESTRATOR_POLICY.md, memory.json, skills.json — its navigate_to BFS-pathfinding skill carries a mutation_history of self-authored code diffs across generations).

Headless client/server: run.py starts a FastAPI game server on --port plus a frame-stream server on port+1, over mGBA (Emerald) or PyBoy (Red); run_cli.py adds an MCP proxy on port+2 so Dockerized Claude Code / Gemini CLI / Codex / Hermes agents play through restricted get_game_state / press_buttons tools.

Four --scaffold tiers matching the paper: simplest and simple (H_min ablations), hand-engineered pokeagent (H_expert: subagent_reflect/verify/battler/planner, A* pathfinding, damage calculator), and continualharness (H_CH); --bootstrap-from resumes a prior run's evolved harness frozen or still-updating, and the same loop extends to weights via an online DAgger + process-reward-model pipeline.
advantages: The only substrate in this catalog where self-improvement happens mid-episode with no resets — gains come from in-context CRUD edits on prompt/sub-agents/skills/memory, not retraining or fresh episodes, cleanly isolating harness-level learning.

Built-in capability-scaling evidence: in the paper it is strictly Pareto-dominant on Gemini 3 Pro, high-variance on Flash, and below the minimalist baseline on Flash-Lite — a ready-made testbed for 'when does refinement help at all?'

Ships a completed run's evolved harness as a bootstrap artifact, so you can study a real mutation history (skill code diffs, prompt self-corrections like the trash-can-puzzle lesson) without running anything.
continual-harness.run: git clone https://github.com/sethkarten/continual-harness && cd continual-harness && uv sync  (Python 3.10–3.11; legally-obtained PokemonRed-GBC/pokered.gbc or Emerald-GBAdvance/rom.gba; backend API key). Then: python run.py --game red --scaffold continualharness --enable-prompt-optimization --optimization-window-length 50 --backend gemini --model-name gemini-3-pro-preview --port 8000 --agent-auto
continual-harness.note: Read EVOLVED_ORCHESTRATOR_POLICY.md first — the prompt a Refiner actually converged to, full of learned lessons. Then trace one evolve() generation in harness_evolver.py against skills.json's mutation_history. Note the capability floor: refinement hurt Flash-Lite.

evoagentx.what: Open-source Python framework (code for arXiv 2507.03616) that generates multi-agent workflows from a natural-language goal, executes them, then optimizes them with pluggable evolution algorithms — TextGrad, AFlow (MCTS), MIPRO, EvoPrompt, SEW, MAP-Elites — scored against built-in benchmarks.
architecture: Generation pipeline in evoagentx/workflow/: WorkFlowGenerator (workflow_generator.py) composes a TaskPlanner (goal to subtasks), an AgentGenerator (assign or create the agent for each subtask) and a WorkFlowReviewer over num_turns refinement iterations, emitting a WorkFlowGraph of nodes/edges (workflow_graph.py); AgentManager.add_agents_from_workflow() instantiates it and WorkFlow.execute() runs it; graphs persist via save_module()/from_file(). Siblings: action_graph.py, controller.py, environment.py, operators.py, workflow_manager.py.

Optimizers in evoagentx/optimizers/, all off a shared optimizer.py base: AFlowOptimizer (ported from MetaGPT's AFlow, MIT) runs MCTS-style rounds where each round_N/ directory holds a candidate graph.py+prompt.py, samples parents from top scores, and checks convergence via ConvergenceUtils; SEWOptimizer (Self-Evolving Workflows) converts a SequentialWorkFlowGraph into python/yaml/code/core/bpmn representations, then mutates them zero- or first-order with mutation prompts from SimplePromptBreeder under optimize_mode structure|prompt|all; plus textgrad, mipro, evoprompt and map_elites optimizers.

Evaluation is first-class: evoagentx/benchmark/ ships loaders for GSM8K, HotPotQA, MBPP, HumanEval, LiveCodeBench, BigBenchHard, NQ, WorfBench and Real-MM-RAG feeding evoagentx/evaluators/ (aflow_evaluator.py); the README reports TextGrad/AFlow/MIPRO deltas on HotPotQA F1, MBPP pass@1 and MATH, and GAIA prompt-optimization of Open Deep Research and OWL.

Execution substrate: evoagentx/tools/ (~30 toolkits — Python/Docker interpreters, BrowserToolkit and LLM-driven BrowserUseToolkit, Google/DDGS/Serper search, ArxivToolkit, FAISS/MongoDB/PostgreSQL, MCP via mcp.py); evoagentx/hitl/ (HITLManager, HITLInterceptorAgent with HITLMode.PRE_EXECUTION approve/reject gating mid-workflow); evoagentx/memory/ (short- and long-term, memory_manager.py, context_manager.py); evoagentx/models/ (OpenAI native plus LiteLLM/openrouter/siliconflow/Qwen).
advantages: The only substrate in this catalog where the search algorithm is a swappable argument rather than the contribution: TextGrad, AFlow-MCTS, MIPRO, EvoPrompt, SEW and MAP-Elites all optimize the same WorkFlowGraph through one Optimizer interface over one benchmark harness, so you can benchmark evolution algorithms head-to-head instead of re-implementing each paper.

Closes the loop from blank page to evolved artifact: natural-language goal to generated WorkFlowGraph to executed workflow to optimizer rounds that literally rewrite graph.py/prompt.py per round (AFlow) or mutate a serialized graph scheme (SEW) — the runnable counterpart to the workflow-evolution papers this catalog otherwise treats as read-only.

Optimizes other people's deployed agents, not just its own: the README demonstrates prompt-optimizing HuggingFace's Open Deep Research and camel-ai's OWL on GAIA, and Wonderful_workflow_corpus/ ships executable workflow.json+tools.json apps (arXiv digest, stock analysis) you can feed straight to the optimizers.
evoagentx.run: pip install evoagentx  (or pip install git+https://github.com/EvoAgentX/EvoAgentX.git). Core loop from the README: WorkFlowGenerator(llm).generate_workflow(goal) → AgentManager().add_agents_from_workflow(graph, llm_config) → WorkFlow(graph, agent_manager, llm).execute(). For evolution: examples/optimization/aflow/aflow_mbpp.py (also hotpotqa/humaneval/math variants), Colab notebooks docs/ColabNotebook/tutorial_notebooks/aflow_optimizer.ipynb and textgrad_optimizer.ipynb.
evoagentx.note: Read evoagentx/optimizers/sew_optimizer.py (scheme round-tripping + mutation prompts) against aflow_optimizer.py (round directories, experience, convergence) — the clearest side-by-side of two workflow-evolution search strategies; then benchmark/ to see how scoring wires in. Pair with the paper's Section 3 for the generation-execution-optimization architecture.

evolver.what: EvolveR — self-evolving LLM agents via an experience-driven lifecycle: rollout trajectories are distilled into guiding/cautionary principles in a Milvus experience DB, retrieved at task time via a <search_experience> action, and outcome scores reinforce a GRPO-trained Qwen2.5-3B policy (arXiv 2510.16079, ICML 2026).
architecture: evolver/experience/experience_manager.py — ExperienceManager.reflection() runs every training step (experience.organize_interval=1): it flushes the trajectory buffer to the VDB, re-scores each retrieved principle with Laplace-smoothed success (success_count+1)/(usage_count+2) in _update_metric_scores(), then _distill_new_experiences() summarizes each trajectory via SUMMARIZE_SUCCESSFUL/FAILED_TRAJECTORY_PROMPT into a [DESCRIPTION] sentence plus [STRUCTURE] (subject, predicate, object) triplets — typed 'guiding' on success, 'cautionary' on failure — dedups candidates with pairwise MATCH_PRINCIPLE_PROMPT yes/no LLM votes over connected components, then merges into an existing principle (embedding-similarity gate + LLM match, linking the source trajectory as a positive/negative example) or creates a new one; principles scoring under clean_low_metric_threshold=0.3 are purged, as are 'collapsed' ('!!!!!') and special-token-contaminated ones caught at retrieval time.

evolver/experience/milvusdb/ — the 'Experience VDB': a FastAPI server (routers/principles.py, trajectories.py, search.py, export_import.py; start_server.sh) over a single-file Milvus DB; scripts/train_grpo-3b.sh installs a trap that POSTs /export/ of the principles+trajectories collections to data/evolver/result/<experiment>/db_exports as jsonl on exit, and scripts/test-3b.sh restores a prior run via VDB_IMPORT_DB_FILE — the evolved memory is a checkpointable, transferable artifact, not transient context.

evolver/llm_agent/generation.py — the multi-turn rollout (max_turns=10) over <think>/<search>/<search_experience>/<answer> actions: a <search_experience> query calls ExperienceManager.retrieve(top_k=3), returning RetrievedExperiencePackage(principle, similarity_score, positive_examples, negative_examples); _build_prompt_with_experience() packs packages into the token budget with priorities 1. principle description + metric_score, 2. structure subgraph, 3. example trajectories; actor state_masking masks the <information>/<experience> observation blocks out of the policy loss.

evolver/rewards/ + vendored verl/ and LLaMA-Factory/ — outcome_reward_fn (exact match for closed QA; weighted F1 + an LLM 'independence/diversity' score for open-ended) drives GRPO via verl.trainer.main_ppo (algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo; default weights format=0.1, outcome=1.0, experience=0); experience_reward_fn can additionally pay merit_score × embedding-similarity for used principles; scripts/cold_start_sft.sh produces the qwen-3b-instruct-cold_start starting checkpoint, and evolver/search/ serves an e5_Flat.index over the wiki-18 corpus (explicit Search-R1 lineage).
advantages: Memory with a trust ledger: every principle carries usage_count/success_count and a smoothed metric_score that decides both survival (purged below 0.3) and retrieval merit — you can watch individual strategies earn and lose the system's trust across training, which prompt-only memory banks (ACE playbooks, Dynamic Cheatsheet) never measure.

Principles are dual-representation and example-grounded: a natural-language description for embedding retrieval plus SPO-triplet structure, each shipping linked successful AND failed trajectories as few-shot evidence at retrieval time — the most concrete artifact in this catalog for studying strategy (not fact) memory.

The lifecycle closes inside the RL loop itself — distill every step, retrieve during rollouts, reinforce from outcomes — rather than wrapping a frozen model; and jsonl export/import lets one experiment's grown memory seed another (VDB_IMPORT_DB_FILE), making memory evolution itself reproducible.

pip install torch==2.4.0 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121
pip3 install vllm==0.6.3
pip install -e .   # installs the vendored verl
pip3 install flash-attn --no-build-isolation

voyager.what: Voyager — code for arXiv 2305.16291: the first LLM-powered open-ended embodied agent in Minecraft, combining an automatic curriculum, an execution-verified code skill library, and iterative prompting with environment feedback and self-verification to learn continuously without gradients.
architecture: voyager/voyager.py — class Voyager is the orchestrator (docstring maps agents to paper components). learn() is the lifelong loop: CurriculumAgent.propose_next_task() → rollout() of at most action_agent_task_max_retries=4 ActionAgent iterations → if CriticAgent confirms success, SkillManager.add_new_skill() commits the JS program; max_iterations=160 default. decompose_task() + inference() replay a learned library on new tasks; ckpt_dir + resume=True restores completed_tasks, failed_tasks, qa_cache and skills from disk.

voyager/agents/curriculum.py — CurriculumAgent (GPT-4 task proposer, gpt-3.5-turbo QA sidekick) proposes 'the next task' from an observation whose fields are revealed progressively by a warm_up dict as completed_tasks grows; task 0 is hard-coded 'Mine 1 wood log', and inventory-full (≥33/36 slots) hard-codes deposit-into-chest / place-chest / craft-chest. A two-step run_qa asks and answers Minecraft questions, cached in ckpt_dir/curriculum/qa_cache.json with a Chroma question vectordb (dedup at similarity score < 0.05).

voyager/agents/skill.py — SkillManager stores each verified skill as {ckpt_dir}/skill/code/<name>.js plus a GPT-written description in description/<name>.txt and skills.json, embedded into a Chroma skill/vectordb; retrieve_skills() injects the top_k=5 description-matched skill sources into the ActionAgent system prompt, and the programs property concatenates every skill with the hand-written mineflayer primitives in voyager/control_primitives/ (exploreUntil.js, craftItem.js, mineBlock.js, killMob.js, smeltItem.js, useChest.js...) that LLM code calls. Re-learning a name versions it (craftIronPickaxeV2.js) rather than overwriting.

voyager/agents/critic.py + voyager/env/ — CriticAgent.check_task_success() renders the event stream (biome, voxels, health/hunger, equipment, inventory, chest contents) and returns {success, critique}; the critique re-enters the ActionAgent's next prompt (auto mode is GPT-4 self-verification; manual mode asks a human). voyager/env/bridge.py, process_monitor.py and the Node side voyager/env/mineflayer/index.js with lib/observation/{status,voxels,inventory,chests,onChat,onError,onSave}.js run the bot and emit those events; prompt templates live in voyager/prompts/ (action_template.txt, curriculum.txt, critic.txt, skill.txt).
advantages: The canonical execution-verified skill library: admission requires critic-confirmed task success, and skills are compositional, interpretable JS (built on named control primitives) that persist across sessions and transfer to a fresh Minecraft world — the reference design every code-as-skill self-improvement loop in this catalog is measured against.

Compounding is inspectable in the shipped artifact: skill_library/trial1 holds ~100 learned skills with V2 rewrites (mineFiveIronOresV2.js, craftIronPickaxeV2.js, craftIronHelmetV2.js) showing iterative self-refinement, and the curriculum's warm_up gating plus qa_cache show how task difficulty and world knowledge scale with competence — readable even without running the game.

Pure in-context lifelong learning: zero gradient updates, blackbox GPT-4 queries only, so skills survive model changes and avoid catastrophic forgetting — a useful counterfactual to weight-update substrates (GRPO/RL substrates in this catalog) for studying what 'improvement' means when only the environment-side artifact grows.

adas.what: ADAS (Automated Design of Agentic Systems) — Meta Agent Search: a meta agent iteratively programs new agents as executable forward() code, scores each on a validation split, and appends survivors to a growing archive of designs (arXiv 2408.08435, ICLR 2025).
architecture: Agent-as-code: every candidate is one complete `def forward(self, taskInfo)` function; `evaluate_forward_fn()` in `_mmlu/search.py` literally `exec()`s the string and installs it via `setattr(AgentSystem, 'forward', func)`, so discovered agents run inside a shared shell whose `LLMAgentBase.query()` returns `Info` namedtuples (name, author, content, iteration_idx).

Per-domain self-contained searches: `_mmlu/`, `_arc/`, `_drop/`, `_gpqa/`, `_mgsm/` each carry a `search.py` + `{domain}_prompt.py`; the archive is seeded by `get_init_archive()` with 7 hand-written agents (COT, COT_SC, Reflexion, LLM_debate, Take_a_step_back, QD, Role_Assignment) and persisted to `results/{expr}_run_archive.json`.

Each generation: `get_prompt(archive)` shows the meta agent the full scored archive plus a placeholder `AgentArchitecture` interface and 'WRONG Implementation examples'; the proposal then goes through two Reflexion revision passes (`get_reflexion_prompt(archive[-1])` feeds back the previous attempt — the repo-level realization of the paper's re-architect step) and an execution-error debug loop (`debug_max=3`) that returns stack traces as `debug_thought`.

Fitness is median + 95% bootstrap CI of accuracy on a 128-example validation slice (`--valid_size 128`, `--n_generation 30`, gpt-4o default); after search, `evaluate()` re-runs every archived agent on the held-out test split, and `_arc/search.py` instead execs a candidate `transform()` function with `run_examples_and_get_feedback()` giving per-example CORRECT/WRONG feedback.
advantages: The cleanest executable-improvement substrate in this catalog: improvements are whole Python programs the meta agent wrote (multi-agent flows, debate, reflection), so the search space is Turing-complete rather than a fixed prompt/prompt-part genome like prompt-optimizers or Darwin-Gödel-style mutation.

Scored archive (not just mutation of one incumbent) makes it the reference setup for studying novelty, stepping stones, and transfer: `_transfer_math/` re-evaluates agents discovered on one domain zero-shot on unseen ones (gsm8k, gsmhard, SVAMP, Asdiv, DROP).

Small enough to fully read in an afternoon — one `search.py` per domain, no framework — so you can trace every loop of a code-level self-improver end to end and re-target it to a new task by editing one `evaluate_forward_fn`.
adas.run: conda create -n adas python=3.11; conda activate adas; pip install -r requirements.txt; export OPENAI_API_KEY="YOUR KEY HERE"; then python {DOMAIN}/search.py with {DOMAIN} in {_arc, _drop, _gpqa, _mgsm, _mmlu} (defaults: 30 generations, gpt-4o-2024-05-13).

Then `_mmlu/mmlu_prompt.py` for the meta prompt (archive, interface, WRONG examples) and Reflexion prompts. Heed the untrusted-code-execution warning; results JSONs are committed under `results/`.

ai-scientist.what: The AI Scientist — an end-to-end ML research loop (idea → experiment → paper → review).
architecture: Idea generation (novelty-checked) → experiments → plots → LaTeX paper → automated reviewer.
Iterates; on the order of ~$15 per paper.
ai-scientist.run: Python; LLM API keys; run the pipeline over a research template (see README).
ai-scientist.note: Run it to see 'AI doing AI research' end to end; read v2 for the agentic-search upgrade.

funsearch.what: FunSearch — LLM + evaluator + evolution that discovered new mathematics (cap sets).
architecture: A frozen LLM proposes candidate functions in a problem skeleton; an evaluator scores them.
The best functions are fed back as few-shot examples (an evolutionary loop).
funsearch.run: Python (Jupyter); provides the evaluator + program-sampler framework.
funsearch.note: The cleanest 'LLM + evaluator' loop — study the evaluate → select → prompt cycle, then run a toy problem.

mlevolve.what: MLEvolve — an agentic MLE system that solves Kaggle-style competitions via progressive Monte Carlo Graph Search with multi-agent collaboration; #1 on MLE-bench (65.3% medal rate, 12h) and best on 11 of 15 math-optimization tasks against five specialized systems including AlphaEvolve (arXiv 2606.06473; AutoMLGen successor).
architecture: Search core — engine/agent_search.py: AgentSearch coordinates the MCGS loop and delegates to engine/node_selection (UCT with _piecewise_decay exploration constant: initial_C=1.414 until T1, linear decay to lower_bound=0.7 by T2 from cfg.agent.decay.phase_ratios; root-locked draft/fusion_draft children), engine/evaluation, engine/execution (Interpreter) and engine/solution_manager; every SearchNode is tagged with a branch_id and tracked in branch_all_nodes/branch_successful_nodes.

Agent suite — agents/: draft/improve/debug plus evolution_agent (intra-branch evolution on stagnation), fusion_agent + aggregation_agent (cross-branch fusion, and multi-branch aggregation when the root hits its draft limit), code_review_agent, data_leakage_agent (metric beyond leakage_max_threshold=0.999 triggers a check); codegen is multi-mode — agents/coder/diff_coder/ SEARCH/REPLACE patching (diff_generate.py, patcher.py, apply.py) vs stepwise_coder.py vs single-pass, dispatched from config flags use_diff_mode/use_stepwise_generation.

Experience memory — agents/memory/global_memory.py: GlobalMemoryLayer persists a MemRecord per node (plan, code summary, stage, success/failure label, parent/current metric, exec_time) into a task-scoped workspace_dir/global_memory dir; agents/memory/retriever.py HybridRetriever fuses BM25Okapi keyword hits with FAISS vector search via Reciprocal Rank Fusion, and agents/planner/planner_with_memory.py uses it for the two-stage retrieval-augmented planning mode.

Stagnation triggers — engine/conditions.py: should_trigger_branch_fusion fires only inside a fusion_min_time_hours–fusion_max_time_hours window (config comment: cross-branch fusion >=6h) when >=fusion_min_branches branches each hold >=fusion_min_successful_nodes successful nodes and is_globally_stagnant is true; is_branch_stagnant counts threshold=3 attempts without beating the branch best; engine/coldstart/ recommends pretrained models per task category from models_guidance_classified.json.
advantages: The most credible open-source data point in this catalog for long-horizon evolutionary search: #1 on MLE-bench at 65.3% medal rate on a 12-hour budget (baselines mostly get 24h), and per the paper it is best on 11/15 math-optimization tasks against five specialized systems including AlphaEvolve (the README's own tables claim matches-or-beats on 14/15) — evidence the substrate generalizes past Kaggle to algorithm discovery.

Cross-branch fusion is a concrete self-improvement mechanism you can read and ablate: on global stagnation the system merges insights from top-performing nodes across different branches into new candidates and runs trajectory-aware evolution over each branch's full improvement history — richer than the flat restart/population loops most evolutionary coder repos ship.

Memory with honest labels and per-agent retrieval policies: every node's plan/code/metric/success-failure outcome is stored and retrieved via hybrid BM25+FAISS (RRF), with different agents querying memory differently to force novel approaches — plus cold-start guidance per task category, all switchable via use_global_memory/use_evolution/use_fusion/use_aggregation ablation flags.

pip install --no-deps -r requirements_ml.txt
pip install --no-deps -r requirements_domain.txt
# edit config/config.yaml: set dataset_dir to the mle-bench data root and agent.code/feedback base_url+api_key (OpenAI-compatible endpoints; if agent.use_global_memory, also set agent.memory_embedding_model_path, and agent.memory_embedding_device: cpu without CUDA)
bash run_single_task.sh <EXP_ID> <DATASET_DIR> [SERVER_ID]
